title: Burnout Trajectory
interpretation: A 14-day pattern showing progressively rising stress scores above 60, declining recovery scores below 40, sleep efficiency dropping below 70%, HRV declining more than 30% from baseline, and daily steps decreasing by 40%+ constitutes a burnout trajectory. This multi-system decline indicates the body and mind are failing to recover from daily demands. The gradual nature makes it invisible day-to-day, but the compound trend is serious.
recommended_agent_action: Escalate to Level 4 alert when all five signals show concurrent negative trends over 14 days. Present user with clear trend visualization. Strongly recommend workload reduction and professional support.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose clinical burnout. This is a trajectory pattern that warrants intervention, not a diagnosis.

title: Stress-Driven Insomnia
interpretation: When elevated daytime stress scores (above 50) consistently precede poor sleep that night (sleep onset above 30 minutes, efficiency below 70%, total hours below 6), this establishes a stress-driven insomnia pattern. The stress keeps the sympathetic nervous system activated, preventing the parasympathetic shift needed for sleep onset. The resulting sleep deprivation increases the next day's stress reactivity, creating a worsening cycle.
recommended_agent_action: Escalate to Level 3 if pattern persists for 5+ days. Suggest evidence-based interventions: wind-down routine, cognitive behavioral techniques for sleep, and daytime stress management. Ask about specific stressors to personalize advice.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose insomnia disorder. Clinical insomnia requires assessment of daytime impairment and exclusion of other causes.
sources: Sleep Medicine Reviews - Stress and Insomnia

title: Overtraining
interpretation: In physically active users, a pattern of consistently high activity intensity combined with rising resting HR, declining HRV, recovery scores below 35, and sleep efficiency below 75% indicates overtraining syndrome. The body is unable to recover between exercise sessions. Paradoxically, performance typically declines despite maintained or increased training volume.
recommended_agent_action: Escalate to Level 3 for active users showing this pattern for 7+ days. Recommend scheduled rest days and reduced training intensity. Suggest the user track subjective fatigue levels.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose overtraining syndrome from data alone. Clinical OTS requires performance testing and exclusion of other causes (illness, psychological stress).
sources: European Journal of Sport Science - Recovery Monitoring

title: Illness Onset Signature
interpretation: The illness onset signature combines: skin temperature rising 0.5-1.0°C above baseline over 1-2 days, resting HR increasing 10-15% above baseline, HRV declining 20%+ from baseline, SpO2 potentially dipping to 95-96%, and recovery score dropping. This multi-signal pattern has been validated in wearable studies to appear 24-48 hours before symptomatic illness onset, providing an early warning opportunity.
recommended_agent_action: If 3+ of these 5 signals trend in illness direction simultaneously, alert user with Level 2 nudge about potential illness onset. Suggest precautionary rest, hydration, and immune support.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose any specific illness. The pattern indicates immune system activation, not a specific pathogen or disease.
sources: Nature Medicine - Pre-Symptomatic COVID Detection via Wearables

title: Cardiac Concern Elderly User
interpretation: In users aged 65+, a sudden combination of: HR above 120 while sedentary, SpO2 below 94%, breathing rate above 20, HRV collapse below 25, and high EDA — especially at night — constitutes the highest severity pattern. This multi-signal acute event in an elderly sedentary user at night is the most concerning pattern the system can detect. Age, time of day, and activity context all amplify the severity.
recommended_agent_action: Immediate Level 5 emergency response. Notify emergency contact instantly. Display emergency alert on all connected devices. Log full telemetry snapshot. This is the highest priority pattern in the system.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose myocardial infarction, stroke, or pulmonary embolism. The pattern demands immediate medical evaluation; the agent does not diagnose.
sources: Lancet Digital Health - Wearable Cardiac Monitoring in Elderly

title: Sleep Apnea Indicators
interpretation: A pattern of nocturnal SpO2 dips below 93% occurring multiple times per night, combined with elevated nocturnal breathing rate, frequent wake episodes (4+ per night), and reduced sleep efficiency below 70%, is consistent with obstructive sleep apnea. The repetitive desaturation-arousal cycle disrupts sleep architecture and has significant cardiovascular consequences if untreated.
recommended_agent_action: If this pattern appears on 5+ nights, escalate to Level 3 and strongly recommend discussion with a healthcare provider about a sleep study. Frame as actionable health optimization, not alarm.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose sleep apnea. Diagnosis requires a formal polysomnography or approved home sleep test. Wearable data provides screening indicators only.
sources: New England Journal of Medicine - Obstructive Sleep Apnea

title: Accumulated Stress Load
interpretation: Seven or more consecutive days with stress scores above personal baseline by 50%+, recovery scores below 35, HRV below baseline by 25%+, sleep under 6 hours with efficiency below 70%, and declining physical activity define an accumulated stress load. Unlike acute stress, accumulated stress load reflects a systemic inability to recover. Every additional day in this state compounds the physiological debt.
recommended_agent_action: Escalate to Level 3. Provide user with a clear week-over-week comparison. Identify the primary contributing factor (sleep, stress, or activity) and suggest targeted intervention. Ask what has changed in their life recently.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude the user is in crisis. Accumulated stress is reversible with appropriate rest, lifestyle adjustment, or stress management.
sources: Journal of Behavioral Medicine - Stress Recovery

title: Anxiety vs Cardiac Differentiation
interpretation: Both anxiety/panic and cardiac events can produce elevated HR, breathing rate, and stress indicators while sedentary. Key differentiators: anxiety typically shows normal or elevated SpO2 (hyperventilation effect), self-limits within 20-30 minutes, and may have been preceded by psychological trigger. Cardiac events more often show SpO2 decline, do not self-resolve, and occur without obvious psychological trigger.
recommended_agent_action: Monitor SpO2 as key differentiator. If SpO2 remains normal and episode resolves within 30 minutes, log as probable anxiety episode. If SpO2 drops or episode persists, escalate as cardiac concern.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not tell the user they are having a panic attack or a cardiac event. Present observations and recommend medical evaluation if uncertain.
sources: American Journal of Emergency Medicine - Panic vs ACS
Annals of Emergency Medicine - Chest Pain Differentiation

title: Pre-Illness Detection Window
interpretation: The 48-hour window before symptomatic illness onset typically shows: HRV declining 15-25%, stress score rising without obvious stressor, sleep efficiency declining, and skin temperature beginning to rise. Catching this window allows for proactive rest that may reduce illness severity and duration.
recommended_agent_action: When 3+ pre-illness signals align within a 48-hour window, send Level 2 nudge suggesting the user's body may be fighting something. Recommend additional rest and hydration.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not state the user is getting sick. Present as possibility worth precautionary action.

title: Good Sleep Poor Recovery Paradox
interpretation: When total sleep hours and sleep efficiency are adequate (7+ hours, 85%+ efficiency) but recovery scores remain low and HRV is suppressed, this paradox suggests sleep quality is inadequate despite adequate quantity. Possible causes include alcohol use (suppresses deep sleep and HRV), sleep-disordered breathing, or psychological stress maintaining sympathetic activation during sleep.
recommended_agent_action: If this paradox persists for 5+ days, flag as insight. Ask about alcohol consumption, screen time before bed, and room environment. Suggest tracking deep sleep percentage trends.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not assume the user is sleeping well just because hours are adequate. Sleep quality and sleep quantity are independent dimensions.
sources: Sleep Medicine - Sleep Quality vs Quantity
Alcohol and Alcoholism - Sleep Architecture Effects

title: Daytime Autonomic Dysregulation
interpretation: Persistent HR elevation above 85 and stress scores above 50 throughout the entire day, even during sedentary periods and meal times when parasympathetic activity should dominate, suggests autonomic nervous system dysregulation. Normal daily patterns show parasympathetic recovery periods throughout the day.
recommended_agent_action: Track the presence of parasympathetic recovery windows during the day (periods where HR and stress normalize). If none occur for 3+ consecutive days, flag as pattern. Suggest intentional relaxation breaks.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose dysautonomia or autonomic neuropathy. This pattern reflects functional autonomic imbalance that is often reversible.

title: Deconditioning Spiral
interpretation: When daily steps drop below 3000 consistently while sleep quality, stress, and recovery all deteriorate, this indicates a deconditioning spiral. Reduced physical activity worsens sleep, which increases stress, which further reduces motivation for activity. Each element feeds the others in a negative cycle.
recommended_agent_action: If step count has dropped 50%+ from baseline concurrent with worsening sleep and stress for 7+ days, gently suggest light walks. Frame physical activity as a recovery tool, not another obligation.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude depression or physical disability from low step counts. Many factors affect daily activity levels.
sources: British Journal of Sports Medicine - Physical Activity Minimum
Preventive Medicine - Sedentary Behavior and Health

title: Expected Post-Vaccination Response
interpretation: In the 24-72 hours after vaccination, elevated HR (+5-15 bpm), reduced HRV (-10-20%), slightly reduced SpO2 (-1-2%), and elevated skin temperature (+0.3-0.8°C) are normal immune responses. These changes are expected and self-resolve. They should not be flagged as illness onset or cardiac concern.
recommended_agent_action: If user has reported recent vaccination, suppress illness onset and cardiac alerts for 72 hours. Log physiological changes as expected immune response. Only escalate if changes exceed expected range or persist beyond 72 hours.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not flag post-vaccination responses as pathological. This is normal immune system activation.

title: Functional Overreaching vs Overtraining
interpretation: Short-term performance decrements with depressed HRV and recovery that resolve within 2 weeks represent functional overreaching — a normal training response that leads to supercompensation. If the same pattern persists beyond 2 weeks despite reduced training, it crosses into non-functional overreaching or overtraining syndrome.
recommended_agent_action: For active users, track HRV and recovery response to training load changes. If reducing training for 1 week does not improve HRV and recovery, escalate concern.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conflate short-term training fatigue with overtraining syndrome. Brief performance dips after hard training blocks are expected and beneficial.

title: Multi-Signal Stress Confirmation
interpretation: When stress_score, EDA (high), heart rate elevation, and skin temperature change all align simultaneously, this represents the highest confidence stress detection. A single elevated signal may be artifactual, but concordance across 3+ independent signals confirms genuine sympathetic activation.
recommended_agent_action: Use multi-signal concordance to weight stress detection confidence. 3+ concordant signals increase confidence above 90%. Use this for decision-making about alert escalation.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not assume concordant stress signals indicate psychological distress. Physical stressors (pain, illness, exertion) produce the same physiological signature.

title: Silent Hypoxia Pattern
interpretation: In elderly users, SpO2 can drop to dangerous levels (below 92%) with minimal increase in breathing rate or subjective awareness — a condition known as silent hypoxia. The body fails to mount an adequate ventilatory response. This makes SpO2 monitoring particularly critical in elderly users as they may not feel breathless despite significant desaturation.
recommended_agent_action: For elderly users, lower the SpO2 alert threshold from 94% to 95%. If SpO2 drops below 92% without corresponding breathing rate increase, this is a Level 5 emergency requiring immediate action.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not assume the user is fine because they are not reporting symptoms. Silent hypoxia is characterized by the absence of subjective symptoms.

title: Recovery After Acute Stress Event
interpretation: After an acute stress event (acute stress scores above 80), the expected recovery timeline is: stress normalizes within 2-4 hours, HR returns to baseline within 1 hour, HRV begins recovering within 6-12 hours, and sleep quality that night may be impacted. Recovery score typically takes 24-48 hours to fully rebound. Faster recovery indicates better stress resilience.
recommended_agent_action: After an acute stress event, monitor recovery timeline. If all metrics return to baseline within 48 hours, log as successful recovery. If recovery is delayed beyond 72 hours, flag as concern.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not judge stress resilience from a single event. Individual recovery patterns vary widely based on context and preparedness.

title: Commute Stress Pattern
interpretation: Elevated HR and stress scores during commute times (typically morning and evening) that consistently spike above baseline may indicate commute-related stress. If commute stress is the primary stress driver, weekends should show markedly better stress and recovery patterns, confirming the association.
recommended_agent_action: If commute-time stress spikes are identified and weekends show significant improvement, note as insight about commute stress contribution. May suggest commute modifications or stress-reducing commute activities.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not assume commute elimination would solve stress problems. Commute stress may be one component of a larger pattern.
sources: BMC Public Health - Commuting and Stress

title: Positive Health Trajectory
interpretation: When HRV shows gradual improvement (10%+ over 30 days), recovery scores trend upward, sleep quality improves, and stress scores trend downward, this constitutes a positive health trajectory. This pattern should be reinforced with positive feedback to maintain motivation. It typically correlates with lifestyle changes the user has made.
recommended_agent_action: Recognize and reinforce positive trends. Share the good news with the user in their preferred communication style. Identify which behavioral changes may be contributing and encourage continuation.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not guarantee continued improvement. Health trajectories can reverse with life changes or seasonal factors.
sources: Health Psychology - Positive Reinforcement in Health Behavior

title: Multi-Signal Baseline Deviation Assessment
interpretation: When assessing any anomaly, the number of concurrent signals deviating from personal baseline determines confidence and severity. Single-signal deviation: likely noise or transient. 2-signal concurrent deviation: notable, begin monitoring. 3-4 signals: pattern forming, likely genuine. 5+ signals: high-confidence event requiring immediate assessment.
recommended_agent_action: Use concurrent signal count as a multiplier for severity assessment. Single signal: observe. 2 signals: log. 3-4 signals: analyze. 5+ signals: act. This framework prevents false positive alerts from single-sensor noise.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not weight all signals equally. Some signals (SpO2, HR) have higher clinical significance than others (skin temperature, EDA) in acute settings.
